correctness.rationale: The claim is true for the stated odd prime and every characteristic-p field. Set R=K[x]/(x^p), A:f(x)↦f(-x), B:f(x)↦f(2x). The truncated logarithm x=log T has invertible linear term and gives the asserted product Af·Bg. For a Leibniz map D set h=D(1); then h=Ah+Bh, so multiplication M_h is itself a twisted-product derivation. D−M_h kills 1; applying Leibniz with 1 on either side shows that it commutes with A and B, after which surjectivity of A and B gives ordinary associative Leibniz. Every such ordinary derivation is u∂x (the relation x^p=0 differentiates to zero). Commuting with A and B forces Au=−u, Bu=2u. These are also the conditions on h: split by the involution A and use invertibility of B to eliminate the +1 part of h. Hence u and h both range over the span of x^(1+jL) for 0≤j<m. Standard commutator identities give exactly the displayed brackets; when i+j≥m the coefficient monomial has exponent ≥p. The H_0 brackets have nonzero factors for all listed E_j and H_j with j>0; no bracket generates H_0. This independently establishes the dimension, basis and derived codimension, including m=1. The supplied script was inspected, not executed; its original-basis modular ranks and finite operator tests reported in VERIFICATION.md are corroboration only.
residual_risks: No replay of the supplied finite checker or formal verification; the universal result was checked algebraically.
